decisions.reason: As a very recent launch with its own webpage and a clear fit with the firm's engineered drainage platform, management is likely to continue it rather than quickly admit the investment was misplaced.
A floor-level shower drainage system sits at the core of the firm's stated move toward accessible, low-profile bathroom drainage, so commitment and strategic fit strongly favor keeping it.
Because this designer shower drainage product was given standalone visibility and supports the firm's design-conscious market position, management would be inclined to persist with it.
The shower element with integrated slope reinforces the firm's integrated installation solution strategy, making withdrawal soon after launch unlikely despite any early uncertainty.
This product was not only presented prominently but explicitly announced as a developed solution, so the public commitment and engineering effort make continued support more likely than exit.

The air-admittance valve appears less central to the firm's main bathroom drainage direction and received only limited website emphasis, but its recent launch still makes management more likely to give it more time than to drop it immediately.
